"Coon," "Sambo," and "darky" were also commonly used racial slurs during this period, often used to perpetuate stereotypes and justify discrimination. These terms are deeply rooted in a history of slavery, segregation, and racial prejudice, and their continued use today can be seen as a reminder of this dark chapter in American history.
